conviction_note: The findings are all small and mostly cancel out (impact_sum -0.5). On the plus side, NatWest has beaten company-compiled consensus four quarters running. On the minus side: FY26 consensus already sits above the company's own guide, Lloyds was sold off today on softer 2027 NII, and the 2027 bank-surcharge rise to 6% has to be quantified. That leaves p_up at 51. abs_move_pct is set at 4.5, well above the 1.7% one-day realised-vol scale, because a guidance change is likely and this is a new quarter with no pre-release. The tiny positive scaled number and the slightly negative findings sum differ in sign only because the beat habit weighs a little more in p_up than its finding does in points. Both are effectively zero.

findings.finding: NatWest has beaten company-compiled consensus every recent quarter: EPS surprise +7.3%, +21.1%, +13.1% and +13.1% over Q3'25-Q2'26. In Q2'26 the pre-Q2 company consensus had EPS at 17.8p and RoTE at 18.4%, and the actual came in at 20.1p and 21.0%, with PBT GBP2.29bn vs GBP2.04bn consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The beats were met with mixed reactions: Q3'25 +4.91%, FY25 -2.49%, Q1'26 -3.35% (guidance hike seen as disappointing), H1'26 +3.22%. On the last eight results days the stock closed up five times.
findings.why_not_priced: Company-compiled consensus has not caught up with a habitual beat: the Q3 range tops out at 20.0p, only 4% above the mean. If a beat were fully expected, the high estimates would cluster above the Q2 actual of 20.1p instead of below it. The beat itself is a pattern, not a sourced Q3 number, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Baseline consensus history (Yahoo earningsHistory) shows the same four beats: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v10/finance/quoteSummary/NWG.L?modules=earningsHistory%2CfinancialData ; AJ Bell confirms the Q2 PBT and income beat: https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/natwest-lifts-2026-guidance-following-evelyn-deal-and-earnings-beat

findings.finding: FY26 consensus is already above the company's own guide: income ex-notables GBP17,997m vs ~GBP17.9bn, and RoTE 19.9% vs >19% (low estimate 18.7%, high 21.4%). The likely guidance raise therefore only has to reach consensus to be a non-event, and Q1'26 is the precedent for a raise that disappointed (-3.35%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance raised at Q3'25: +4.91%. Raised at Q1'26 but judged too small: -3.35%. Raised at H1'26 by more than the street expected: +3.22%.
findings.why_not_priced: Preview copy compares the print with the published guide, which looks easy to beat, rather than with the consensus, which is already above it. If the market were reading the bar off consensus, a mechanical raise to ~GBP18.0bn would already be framed as neutral in previews. Kept small because it is an inference about how the guide will be read.
findings.independence: H1 RNS outlook text, which sets the ~GBP17.9bn and >19% guide: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/natwest-group--nwg/natwest-group-plc-interim-results-2026-part-1/9697081

findings.finding: Lloyds, NatWest's closest UK-domestic peer, reported Q3 today. It kept 2026 guidance but said NII would be only 'modestly above' GBP14.9bn, that 2027 NII growth is 'likely to be lower than in 2026', that mortgage competition is fierce and that deposit-market growth is slow. LLOY closed -5.3% (103.9 -> 98.4p), while NWG fell only -1.4% (646.8 -> 638.0p) in sympathy.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history for a peer read-through. Q1'26 (-3.35%) shows NWG is sold when the forward income trajectory underwhelms.
findings.why_not_priced: NWG has given back about a quarter of Lloyds' move, so part of this is priced. The rest depends on NatWest's own 2027 colour tomorrow. Net of the company, this is a counterparty statement, not NatWest's: NatWest's public hedge guide (+>GBP1.0bn in 2027) is a bigger relative tailwind than Lloyds', which caps the size.
findings.independence: HL on Lloyds Q3, with income slightly light, 2027 forecasts trimmed and 'fierce competition': https://www.hl.co.uk/shares/share-research/lloyds-q3-results-steady-quarter-on-track-for-2026 ; Barclays Q3 income GBP7.4bn vs GBP7.6bn expected, shares flat: https://ground.news/article/barclays-q3-earnings-snapshot

findings.finding: The Budget doubles the bank surcharge from 3% to 6% for 15 months from January 2027, with about 85% of NatWest's profits eligible. Consensus models dated 20 October predate it, and tomorrow is the first time NatWest quantifies the hit. My estimate is roughly GBP0.2-0.25bn of 2027 tax, about 3-4% of the GBP6.56bn consensus attributable profit, or about 0.7pp of 2027 RoTE.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NWG fell about 2% on 16 Oct on reports of a surcharge rise, the UK banks fell 6-11% in October on the 8% fear, and NWG rallied +2.0% on Budget day when the rise came in at 6%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the rate, its duration and the relief rally are all public. What is left is whether management trims the 2027/2028 RoTE framing (2028 >18%) or absorbs the cost. A trim would be new, but the market has already done the arithmetic, so the size is small.
findings.independence: Krugman Insights / Sharecast on 85% profit eligibility and the Budget rally: https://www.krugmaninsights.com/desk-notes/781-a-budget-bank-tax-targets-85-of-lloyds-profits ; https://www.sharecast.com/news/risers-and-fallers/autumn-budget-standard-chartered-banks-lloyds-natwest-barclays--23940603.html

findings.finding: The rate path has turned higher than the one NatWest's H1 outlook assumed (Bank Rate 'held at the current level of 3.75%'). The BoE held at 3.75% on 17 Sep 2026 by 6-3, with three members voting for 4%, and a November hike is live. Consensus averages an end-2026 Bank Rate of 3.91%, with a high of 4.39%. NatWest's 6-year USD senior notes priced at 5.908% on 14 Oct, which shows elevated term yields, and higher swap rates lift structural-hedge reinvestment and deposit margins.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NWG traded as a rate-sensitive name through 2024-26, rising on higher-for-longer. No clean print-day measure.
findings.why_not_priced: This is macro-to-company transmission, so it is sized small. Rates are public, and much of the consensus already carries a 3.91% end-2026 rate. The only unpriced part is whether management turns it into higher 2027 income colour. Offsetting it, higher rates plus an energy shock raise impairment risk (H1 base case unemployment 5.5%).

findings.finding: On 14 Oct 2026 NatWest priced USD1bn of 5.908% senior callable fixed-to-fixed reset notes due 2032 to fund its general banking business. This is routine MREL/senior issuance, not distress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Routine NatWest senior issuance (e.g. the 16 Jun 2026 pricing) has never moved the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing to price: the issuance funds a balance sheet that consensus expects to grow (loans GBP444.6bn Q3E vs GBP439.5bn Q2), and it says nothing about the print.

findings.finding: NatWest said at H1 that its 'next share buyback announcement [will] be with our FY 2026 results'. Q3 therefore carries no buyback, unlike Barclays, which announced GBP500m at its Q3 on 22 Oct. The company consensus has no Q3 buyback (FY26E GBP468m average, to be announced at FY).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Capital-return surprises have moved UK banks on results days, but none is possible here by the company's own statement.
findings.why_not_priced: Already priced: the company itself guided the timing. It is filed so that a reader sees no capital-return upside on this print.

baseline_tension: The findings net slightly negative (-0.5) against a slightly positive priced lean (+0.33) and a -2.2% 20-day / -10.7% 60-day run-up. The drawdown is mostly the surcharge fear, which the Budget has partly unwound. The evidence neither confirms nor clearly opposes the lean, so p_up stays near 50.

'A verified fact is not a predicted reaction': the beat-habit finding was cut from +0.6 to +0.4, because NWG's reactions to its beats are mixed (5 of the last 8 results days up, Q1'26 -3.35% on a raise), and p_up was moved from 52 to 51
